message.content:
Can you help me draft a power of attorney document tailored to my needs?

Yes — I can help. Below is a clear, comprehensive, and reproducible example showing how to draft a simple durable power of attorney tailored to common needs. Use this as a template and adapt language, names, dates, and powers to your jurisdiction and circumstances. Consider having an attorney review the final document.

Example: Durable Power of Attorney (General template)

1. Heading and identification
- Title: Durable Power of Attorney
- Date: [Insert date]
- Principal: [Full legal name of the person granting authority], born [DOB], residing at [address].
- Agent (Attorney-in-Fact): [Full legal name of the person you appoint], born [DOB], residing at [address].

2. Statement of grant of authority
I, [Principal name], hereby appoint [Agent name] as my attorney-in-fact (Agent). This durable power of attorney grants my Agent the authority to act for me in all matters described below, subject to any limitations stated in this document.

3. Effective date and durability
This power of attorney becomes effective immediately upon execution and shall not be affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity. This power of attorney shall continue in effect until my death unless I revoke it earlier in writing.

4. Powers granted
I grant my Agent the authority to make decisions and take actions on my behalf in the following areas (check or specify those that apply; you may limit or expand as needed):
- Real property transactions: buy, sell, mortgage, lease, manage real estate owned by me.
- Personal property transactions: sell, lease, or manage personal property.
- Banking and financial transactions: access accounts, deposit and withdraw funds, endorse checks, open or close accounts, invest funds.
- Business operations: operate, buy, sell, or dissolve any business entity in which I have an interest.
- Tax matters: prepare, sign, and file tax returns; represent me before tax authorities.
- Insurance matters: manage, purchase, maintain, or claim benefits under insurance policies.
- Retirement and benefits: manage retirement accounts, pensions, and social security matters.
- Claims and litigation: initiate, defend, or settle claims on my behalf.
- Personal and family maintenance: make payments for my care, support, education, and maintenance of my dependents.
- Medical decision-making (if desired and allowed under local law): make health-care decisions if I am incapacitated (note: some jurisdictions require a separate health-care power of attorney or advance directive).

5. Limitations and special instructions
- [Optional: Insert any limits, conditions, or exclusions here. For example: “Agent may not sell the principal’s primary residence without the consent of [Name].”]

6. Nomination of guardian (optional)
If a court determines a guardian of my estate or person is necessary, I nominate [Name] to serve as guardian.

7. Agent compensation and liability
- Compensation: The Agent may be compensated for reasonable expenses and services as allowed by law or as agreed in writing.
- Liability: The Agent shall act in good faith and in my best interests. The Agent is not liable for actions taken in good faith.

8. Successor agents
If my named Agent is unable or unwilling to serve, I appoint [Successor Agent name] as successor Agent, to serve with the same powers.

9. Revocation
I retain the right to revoke this power of attorney at any time by providing written notice to my Agent.

10. Signatures and notarization
- Principal’s signature: ___________________________ Date: __________
- Agent’s acceptance (optional but recommended): I, [Agent name], accept the appointment as Agent and agree to serve under the terms of this power of attorney. ___________________________ Date: __________
- Witnesses: Some jurisdictions require witnesses. If so, add signature lines for two witnesses with printed names, addresses, and dates.
- Notary acknowledgment: Many states require or recommend notarization. Include a notary block appropriate for your state.

Sample filled excerpt
- Date: March 1, 2026
- Principal: Maria Gonzalez, DOB 1980-05-14, 123 Oak St., Anytown, State ZIP
- Agent: Javier Morales, DOB 1978-10-02, 456 Pine Ave., Anytown, State ZIP
- Powers granted: All banking and financial transactions; real property transactions; personal property transactions; tax matters.
- Limitations: Agent shall not sell the principal’s primary residence without written consent from the principal.

Practical steps to finalize
1. Customize the template to reflect the specific powers you want to grant or restrict.
2. Verify whether your state requires separate forms, specific language, or witness/notary requirements for a durable power of attorney.
3. Discuss the appointment with the person you plan to name as Agent so they understand their responsibilities.
4. Sign the document in the presence of required witnesses and a notary (if required).
5. Provide copies to your Agent, attorney, and any financial institutions or other third parties that will rely on the document. Keep the original in a safe but accessible place.

If you want, tell me the state or country where you live and the specific powers you want to grant or limit, and I can produce a more tailored draft using local required language and formalities.
